summary: Feed s143_double to IDS is degraded: 21.5% of TCP sessions are one-way (IDS requires bidirectional) and 58.0% of frames are VXLAN-encapsulated, hiding inner traffic from inspection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding only one direction of many flows to this IDS tool port - likely asymmetric routing not aggregated or SPAN/TAP feeds from opposite directions sent to different tools without flow-aware aggregation.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true for stateful TCP reassembly and signature matching; 41 of 191 sessions (21.5%) are unidirectional so IDS cannot reconstruct streams, misses handshakes, and will fail to detect attacks that span request/response.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same IDS tool port with flow-aware hashing so the IDS sees complete bidirectional sessions for stateful detection.

findings.root_cause: Traffic is forwarded encapsulated in VXLAN (1515 of 2610 frames, 58%) and not stripped by the packet broker before delivery, so the IDS sees only outer tunnel headers.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS with needs_full_payload=true cannot inspect inner L2-L7 headers/payloads or apply signatures; tunneled traffic bypasses detection, creating major coverage blind spot.

recommended_fix.why: Terminate/strip VXLAN headers on the packet broker and forward inner frames to the IDS so it can parse inner IP/TCP and payloads for detection.
